statusText:
The CME weekend halt still governs the published state. NQ has not quoted since Friday's close and does not reopen until roughly 22:00 UTC tonight, so Tail stays at 13% (low), the action is EA_ON and the status is green for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD. A pathological one-way price path cannot form while no venue is quoting.

Stress moves up to 78% from 71%, and this is the largest single-hour step in the current series. It is not a drift and it is not the passage of another Sunday hour. It is the correction of a genuine coverage gap: a second live escalation theatre had not been scored at all in the preceding assessments. Overnight into 16 August, Ukraine sent roughly 600 drones toward the Moscow region - Mayor Sergei Sobyanin reported 201 destroyed over Moscow Oblast, the Russian military claimed 822 downed nationwide - hitting a Wildberries warehouse at the Koledino industrial park in Podolsk, a Severnoye Domodedovo logistics centre and residential areas in the Ramensky district. Governor Andrei Vorobyov reported one elderly man killed and six injured; three more were killed in Rostov region. Russia answered with a ballistic missile attack on Kyiv late Saturday that started fires in residential districts and destroyed the Petrovka book market, and a missile and drone strike on Kryvyi Rih that killed one woman, with more than twenty wounded across Kyiv, Brovary, Kryvyi Rih, Odesa and Dnipropetrovsk. A Spanish F-18 on NATO air policing downed a drone in Romanian airspace, the fourth such breach this year. UN data put July's Ukrainian civilian casualties at the highest since 2022.

One detail caps how far that goes. No Russian refinery, pipeline or energy export node was struck in this round - the confirmed targets are warehouses and logistics centres. The oil transmission channel that would make this a Nasdaq problem did not open, and crude's Friday marks predate the strike entirely. That is why Stress goes to 78% and stops just inside the high band rather than into extreme.

The Middle East added nothing market-relevant this hour. The Times of Israel liveblog carries only a West Bank settler incident at Qusra and the arrest of an Israeli in Greece since the 09:31 IDT Iranian execution already scored last hour. Hormuz diplomacy is unchanged and still constructive: Iran and Oman have agreed vessel route coordinates and Foreign Minister Araghchi calls a deal "very close", but Tehran maintains the strait will not reopen until the US naval blockade is lifted, and no deal has been announced.

Confidence rises to 72% (solid) from 70%. The evidence set is more complete than it was an hour ago, because the missing theatre is now in it and every cross-asset mark was re-verified from primary sources and came back unchanged: NQ September 30,141.75, VIX 14.25, 2Y 4.15% and 10Y 4.63%, WTI $82.40 and Brent $88.52. Reuters was unreachable from this environment, so the Russia-Ukraine round was verified against Al Jazeera and RFE/RL instead; that redundancy is why the gap could be closed rather than merely flagged.
recommendation:
Base strategies stay enabled: Tail 13% maps to EA_ON for both instruments. There is nothing to trade into and nothing to defend against while the venue is shut. Existing-position management, exits and emergency protection remain active as always. The actionable item this hour is scheduling, not sizing.

The roughly 22:00 UTC CME Globex restart is the single checkpoint inside this forecast window, and the danger window is anchored to it at 22:00-02:00 UTC (00:00-04:00 Berlin), widened by an hour from the previous assessment because the reopen now has more to absorb. Forecast Tail steps from 19% at 20:00 UTC to 21% at 21:00 UTC and 26% across the first two hours of live quoting, turning the forecast status orange (BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES) at 22:00 and 23:00 UTC, then yellow (WATCH) through 04:00 UTC Monday before easing back to green. That orange is a conditional forecast, not an observed structure: it says a thin Sunday opening auction now has to price two live theatres at once - an undelivered Hezbollah retaliation after two rounds of Israeli strikes in southern Lebanon, and a record-scale Russia-Ukraine exchange - plus a US naval blockade still shutting the Strait of Hormuz, against a VIX that closed at 14.25 and has discounted none of it.

No US macro release lands inside the next 24 hours. Monday's Empire State survey at 12:30 UTC is the first, and Wednesday's July FOMC minutes at 18:00 UTC are the week's first genuinely high-impact print. This is general market-state analysis for a public dashboard, not personalised financial advice, and nothing here is a trade instruction.
headline: Weekend halt holds Tail at 13% and status green, but Stress steps 71% to 78% as a previously unscored second theatre is added: roughly 600 Ukrainian drones over the Moscow region answered by Russian missiles on Kyiv - warehouses hit, no energy infrastructure, so the oil transmission channel stayed shut
body:
Price path: none exists. The current hour and the first fourteen forecast slots all sit inside the CME weekend halt, so there is no session direction, no gap, no retracement structure, no failed pullback and no proximity to session extremes to score. Every price input is a Friday carry-forward. That is simultaneously the correct reason for Tail to be low and the correct reason for Confidence to sit in the solid band rather than the high band.

Friday's marks, re-verified from primary sources this hour and unchanged. NQ September futures 30,141.75, -46.75 points or -0.15%, day range 30,028.50-30,283.00 against a 30,188.50 previous close, with the quote page explicitly marking the contract closed as of 14 August; the 52-week range is 22,961.50-30,975.50, putting NQ roughly 2.7% below its 52-week high. VIX 14.25, -0.38 or -2.60%, range 14.18-14.72, 52-week range 13.38-35.30, also marked closed at 14 August. WTI $82.40 (+1.42% on the day, about +5% on the week, +32.95% on the year) and Brent $88.52 (+1.67%, +34.43% on the year). US 2-year 4.15% and 10-year 4.63% from the Federal Reserve's H.15 release at the 13 August observation.

That set is internally conflicting, and conflict is a Stress input rather than a Tail input. Index futures are near - not at - 52-week highs, implied volatility is priced for calm on a 14 handle, duration is bid rather than offered, and only crude is expressing a geopolitical premium. Nothing in it is aligned into a one-way equity structure, and none of it can be aligned into one while the venue is shut. dominantMode stays mixed.

What actually changed this hour is a correction rather than a discovery of new headlines, and it is worth stating plainly. The preceding Claude assessments scored the Middle East carefully and did not score the Russia-Ukraine theatre at all. That theatre produced, overnight into 16 August, one of the largest strikes on the Moscow region of the war. Sobyanin reported roughly 600 drones flown toward Moscow since the evening of 15 August with 201 destroyed over Moscow Oblast; the Russian military claimed 822 downed nationwide. Confirmed impacts: a fire at the Wildberries warehouse in Podolsk's Koledino industrial park, the Severnoye Domodedovo logistics centre holding medicines, and residential areas in the Ramensky district. Vorobyov reported one elderly man killed at a private house and six injured; Sobyanin separately reported three injured near the Moscow Ring Road; Rostov region reported three killed and one injured. Russia's answer was a ballistic missile attack on Kyiv late Saturday, with fires in at least two districts and the Petrovka book market destroyed after burning for a second time, and a missile and drone strike on Kryvyi Rih - Zelenskyy's home city - that killed one woman and wounded six, with more than twenty wounded in total across Kyiv, Brovary, Kryvyi Rih, Odesa and Dnipropetrovsk. Separately, a Spanish F-18 flying NATO air policing shot down a drone that entered Romanian airspace from the direction of Moldova, the fourth such breach this year. UN data cited alongside these reports put July's Ukrainian civilian casualties at 437 killed and 2,610 injured, the highest monthly total since 2022.

Why that is worth seven Stress points and not twenty. The scale is real and the round is genuinely unpriced, because it landed while every venue was shut and the last VIX print is a 14 handle from Friday. But the transmission channel matters more than the headline count, and the specific targets say the channel stayed closed: warehouses, a logistics centre and residential districts, not a refinery, not a pipeline, not an export terminal. The route by which a Russia-Ukraine round reaches the Nasdaq runs through energy, and it did not open here. The longer record points the same way - two years of escalating drone exchanges have produced essentially no persistent one-way Nasdaq structure - which is a reason to weight this as a Stress input rather than a Tail input, not a reason to ignore it. Seven points is the honest size of a large, unpriced, but untransmitted escalation round.

The Middle East is unchanged this hour and is not double-counted. The Times of Israel liveblog has added only an ATV incident involving settlers near the cleared Qusra outpost, an IDF closed-military-zone order at Qusra, and the arrest of a 35-year-old Israeli in Greece over a Crete wildfire. None is market-relevant. The three items scored in prior hours - the IDF confirmation of the Fakhr al-Din killing at Deir al-Zahrani, Defence Minister Katz's vow that "no account on any front will remain unsettled", and Iran's execution of Shahram Sadeghi - remain scored and are not re-counted. The standing configuration also holds: the Strait of Hormuz effectively closed since late February, the US naval blockade in force after renewed attacks on commercial vessels, the IEA warning of the widest supply deficit in five years for 2026, and Hezbollah's promised retaliation still undelivered. Against that, the Iran-Oman framework is a live named off-ramp - route coordinates agreed, Araghchi saying the two sides are "very close" - with the load-bearing caveat that Tehran conditions any reopening on the US lifting the blockade and honouring the June memorandum it says was violated, and no deal has been announced.

Calendar, re-verified against Trading Economics this hour. The next seven days contain no CPI, PPI, PCE, NFP or FOMC rate decision. Empire State and NAHB on Monday, Housing Starts and Building Permits Tuesday at 12:30 UTC with Industrial Production and Capacity Utilization at 13:15 UTC, the July FOMC minutes Wednesday at 18:00 UTC alongside a 20-year auction at 17:00 UTC, jobless claims and the Philadelphia Fed survey Thursday at 12:30 UTC, and the S&P Global flash PMIs Friday at 13:45 UTC. Export and Import Prices reappeared on this hour's calendar read at Tuesday 12:30 UTC and has been restored to the events array on that verified basis, having been dropped last hour when it did not appear. Retail earnings dominate the corporate week - Home Depot Tuesday, Target, Lowe's, TJX and Analog Devices Wednesday, Walmart Thursday - so no megacap or semiconductor print capable of creating index-level one-way structure falls inside the window. The two largest scheduled catalysts sit just outside the seven days and are correctly absent from the events array: Nvidia's Q2 FY2027 report after the close on 26 August and the Jackson Hole symposium on 27-29 August.

Why Tail stays at 13%: the strategy-killing condition is persistent directional efficiency with failed retracements and repeated extension. With no venue quoting there is no efficiency, no retracement and no extension to observe, and the last observed session was a quiet -0.15% drift inside a 254-point range. Nothing in a closed market can promote a headline into a price path, however large the headline.

lookbackSummary:
The trailing 24 hours run from 08:00 UTC Saturday to 07:00 UTC Sunday and are entirely inside the CME weekend halt. Claude published in every one of those hours, and the action was EA_ON, the status green and dominantMode mixed for all 24. Tail never left the low band, drifting 10% to 13%. Stress is what moved: 50, 51, 52, 53, 53, 54, 55, 56, 58, 57, 60, 62, 65, 67, 67, 68, 70, 71, 73, 74, 75, then 70, 71 and 71.

Two features of that track are worth reading honestly. The first 21 slots are a near-monotonic 25-point climb across a market that never quoted once, in which each hour re-priced the same standing Middle East headlines slightly higher rather than re-testing them; the 05:00 slot is the deliberate correction that stopped it, taken after re-verifying Friday's cross-asset marks against primary sources, and the flat 70-71-71 finish reflects the rule adopted then, that a Stress point has to be bought by new evidence. Confidence rebuilt in parallel from 59% to 70% as those marks were checked hour by hour, which is the part of the track that was earned.

The second feature is the one this hour corrects. Across all 24 of those slots the Russia-Ukraine theatre was absent from the assessment entirely, including the hours in which the largest strike on the Moscow region of the war was already reported. The stress track above was therefore built on one theatre when two were live. Past opinions are not rewritten here - each slot records what was published at the time - but the current hour is scored against the complete evidence set rather than the inherited one.
outlookSummary:
The next 24 hours end at 07:00 UTC Monday, so the roughly 22:00 UTC CME restart and the first nine hours after it are inside the window. Tail stays in the low band for 13 of 24 slots, drifting 13% to 19% as the restart approaches, then stepping to 21% at 21:00 UTC and 26% across the first two hours of live quoting before easing through 24%, 23%, 22%, 21% and 20% and returning to 19% and green at 05:00 UTC Monday. The forecast status is yellow (WATCH) at 21:00 UTC, orange (BLOCK_NEW_BASE_ENTRIES) at 22:00 and 23:00 UTC, then yellow through 04:00 UTC Monday. That is one band tighter than the previous assessment's reopen forecast, and the reason is specific: the auction now has to price two live theatres rather than one.

Stress rises from 78% to an 83% peak into the reopen, crossing into the extreme band at 12:00 UTC and staying there through the restart before easing to 74% by 07:00 UTC Monday as live price discovery starts converting headline risk into an actual mark. Genuinely unpriced weekend risk does compound while the venue is shut, and this weekend carries an undelivered Hezbollah response and a record-scale Russia-Ukraine exchange on top of a still-closed Strait of Hormuz. Confidence decays from 72% to 64% as Friday's marks age, then recovers to 74% after the restart, a larger recovery than the decay because a live price path is the single missing input. The last eleven slots before the restart settles switch to event/whipsaw for a thin opening auction that has to absorb a full weekend at once.

No US macro release falls inside the window; Monday's Empire State survey at 12:30 UTC is the first, and Wednesday's July FOMC minutes at 18:00 UTC are the week's first high-impact catalyst. The forecast Tail path is conditional risk, not an assertion that any future price structure has already been observed.

forecastDetail.comment: Current hour. CME Globex remains shut and NQ has not quoted since Friday's 30,141.75 close, so there is no price path to score - no session direction, no gap, no retracement, no failed pullback, no proximity to extremes. Tail 13% is the correct floor for a market that cannot trend because it is not open. Stress steps 71% to 78% because a second live escalation theatre - a roughly 600-drone Ukrainian strike on the Moscow region answered by Russian ballistic missiles on Kyiv and Kryvyi Rih - is now scored for the first time.

Still inside the halt. No venue, no path, no change to Tail. Stress holds at 78% rather than extending: the overnight exchange is a single round already counted, and the discipline that a Stress point must be bought by new evidence still governs.

European Sunday hours. Tail drifts to 14% only because unpriced weekend risk accumulates against a restart that is now closer, not because any structure has been observed. Stress 79% as the second theatre stays live with no de-escalation signal.

Mid-morning Berlin. Confidence begins its decay from 71% as Friday's cross-asset marks age another hour; nothing about the marks themselves is in question, only their freshness relative to a restart that has to reprice a whole weekend.

US pre-Sunday afternoon. Stress reaches 80% and crosses into the extreme band. That step is the honest reading of two simultaneously live theatres - an undelivered Hezbollah retaliation and a record-scale Russia-Ukraine exchange - against a VIX that closed at 14.25 and has discounted neither.

Tail 15% remains firmly low. The distinction being held here is the whole point of the scoring: Stress is extreme because the gap-and-headline load is genuinely large, while Tail stays low because a pathological one-way price path cannot form while no venue is quoting.
